test_title: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper (Held On: 12th September 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which feature gives the Elephanta Caves their distinct identity among early Indian rock-cut monuments?

options.text: Their reliefs mainly depict Vaishnavite avatars
Strong Shaivite sculptures using depth and contrast
Earliest Buddhist vihara layout in the region
Monolithic carvings from the Sunga era

solution:
The correct answer is __**Strong Shaivite sculptures using depth and contrast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Elephanta Caves** are located on Elephanta Island near Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
 
• These caves are significant for their **Shaivite sculptures** that depict themes from **Hindu mythology**, particularly related to Lord Shiva.
 
• The sculptures in the caves exhibit **exceptional depth and contrast**, highlighting the artistic brilliance of early Indian rock-cut architecture. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• The most prominent sculpture is the **Trimurti**, which represents the three aspects of Shiva: Creator, Preserver, and Destroyer.
 
• The caves are believed to date back to the **5th to 8th century CE**, showcasing the development of Indian art and architecture during that period. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• Although the caves have religious and mythological significance, they primarily emphasize **Shaivism** through intricate carvings rather than Vaishnavism or Buddhism. *Hence, statement 1 and 3 are incorrect.*
 
• The carvings are not monolithic creations from the **Sunga era**; instead, they belong to the later period and are made with a focus on depth and details. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• The **Elephanta Caves** were built during the period of **Gupta or Chalukya rule**, symbolizing the patronage of art and architecture in ancient India.
 
• These caves were declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1987** due to their historical and cultural significance.
 
 
 
• **Trimurti Sculpture:**
 
 
• This is the most iconic sculpture in the caves, showing Shiva as the **Creator, Preserver, and Destroyer**.
 
• The sculpture is approximately **6 meters (20 feet) tall** and exhibits remarkable detail and depth.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features:**
 
 
• The caves are carved out of solid basalt rock and consist of **halls, pillars, and reliefs**, showcasing the expertise of ancient artisans.
 
• The artwork emphasizes **symmetry, proportion, and intricate detailing**, making it unique among Indian rock-cut monuments.
 
 
 
• **Shaivite Influence:**
 
 
• The sculptures primarily focus on **Shaivism**, depicting various forms and aspects of Shiva, including **Ravana lifting Kailash** and **Shiva as Nataraja**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Rock-Cut Monuments:**

 
 
• The **Ajanta and Ellora Caves**, near Aurangabad, Maharashtra, focus on Buddhist and Jain themes, whereas the Elephanta Caves emphasize **Shaivite themes**.
 
• Unlike the early **Buddhist vihara layouts**, Elephanta Caves prioritize sculptural depth and contrast in their depictions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Elephanta Caves:**
 
 
• The caves serve as a testament to the **religious and artistic expression** of ancient India.
 
• They attract thousands of tourists annually and are considered a symbol of **India's cultural heritage**.
